question: In the Medicore procurement email thread about data use and telemetry, what turnaround timeline did Redwood propose for delivering the operational runbook?

gold_documents.text:
Telemetry opt-out, prompt/response ownership and telemetry routing (Medicore)

From: Alex Rivera <alex@medicore.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on data use: telemetry, ownership and KMS residency

Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement we need confirmation on a few items for our security & legal teams so they can sign off: 

1) Do you commit that Medicore prompts and responses will not be used to improve model weights (no-training) unless we explicitly opt in?
2) Can you provide a telemetry opt-out (no-telemetry) so that operational telemetry tied to our tenant is excluded from metric capture and experimentation?
3) We require onshore KMS for key management and evidence that any subprocessor with access to plaintext is located in the US or EU (list and residency).
4) What proof can you provide for deletion requests and audit logs (pattern we expect: timestamped deletion, confirmation, and exportable audit bundle)?

I've attached Medicore_DPA_questions.pdf with redline requests. Can you route to the right people and let me know an estimated timeline?

Appreciate it —
Alex Rivera
Director, Procurement
Medicore Health

(attachment: Medicore_DPA_questions.pdf)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@medicore.com>
Cc: david_kim <david@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data use: telemetry, ownership and KMS residency

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We're aligned with Medicore's security posture and have options to meet each ask; below is a short operational summary. I'll loop in David (ops) and Karthik (policy/legal) for detail and timing.

High-level answers: 
- No-training: Yes — we offer an explicit contract clause and a tenant-level runtime flag that prevents requests from being routed into any model-improvement pipelines. This is available for Hosted and Dedicated modes.
- Telemetry opt-out: We can suppress tenant-identifying telemetry and provide an opt-out mode that still allows anonymized system health signals. Telemetry for billing (token counts) can be provided in aggregate only.
- KMS residency: We support onshore KMS integrations (customer-managed) for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted customers can use onshore KMS via dedicated capacity or private deployment options.
- Proof of deletion & audit: We can export an audit bundle (timestamped events, deletion confirmations, subprocessor access logs) and provide a signed attestation.

Action items from our side:
1) David to propose an ops runbook (how opt-out is enforced at runtime + latency/throughput implications).
2) Karthik to propose contract language and a short redline that covers audit granularity and export.
3) Naomi to provide the current subprocessor inventory and residency matrix.

Would Medicore be ok with a 5-business-day turnaround for the runbook and 7–10 business days for the redline & evidence pack?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference


From: david_kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex@medicore.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data use: telemetry, ownership and KMS residency

Alex / team —

Below is an operational summary to make the commitments concrete. Attaching the current subprocessor inventory for your review.

Runtime enforcement (no-training + telemetry opt-out):
- Tenant flag: We have a per-tenant runtime flag "no_model_learning" instantiated at request ingress. When set, the request path bypasses any learning/experimentation endpoints and writes only into ephemeral caches with a TTL of 1 hour (configurable by agreement).
- KV cache & prefix caching: For latency-sensitive workloads we still use ephemeral KV caches; these are not persisted to training pipelines.
- Telemetry: We separate telemetry into billing metrics (aggregated token counts) and telemetry-flags for health/debug. Opt-out removes tenant-id from all non-billing telemetry streams and writes anonymized buckets to a separate retention pipeline.
- Audit & deletion flow: Deletion request triggers: (1) mark items as deleted (index), (2) purge ephemeral caches and permanent logs within 24 hours, (3) generate exportable audit bundle (jsonL events) including request ids and timestamps. We retain a signed attestation for 12 months by default.

Subprocessors & residency: See attached subprocessor_inventory.csv — columns: name, role, region, access_level. We are able to provide onshore-only routing for traffic (us-east, us-west) and to constrain data plane so only onshore subprocessors handle plaintext when requested.

Latency/throughput considerations: Enforcing no-learning and telemetry opt-out has negligible steady-state latency (<5 ms p50 impact) but may affect our ability to use low-cost experimental batching for some multi-tenant pools. For guaranteed throughput & subprocessor isolation we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) for Medicore's production traffic.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal runbook (this week): PRD that details the runtime flag, expected SLO impact, and rollback plan.
- Evidence package (7 business days): subprocessor manifests, audit bundle sample, and SOC 2 link.

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

(attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex@medicore.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data use: telemetry, ownership and KMS residency

Alex / Vivek —

Legal & compliance notes and suggested contract language: 

1) No-training clause (suggested): "Provider shall not use Customer Data (prompts, completions, or derivatives) to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models or model weights, except with Customer's prior written consent." 

2) Telemetry opt-out (suggested): "Provider shall not collect or retain telemetry that can be used to re-identify Customer tenants or end users. Provider may collect anonymized operational metrics for platform health, provided such metrics are aggregated and cannot be reversed to identify Customer data."

3) Audit & deletion: Include an SLA for audit bundle delivery (e.g., 7 business days) and confirm the export format (we'll provide JSONL + signed hash). Also include attestations for proof-of-deletion.

4) Subprocessor residency & restrictions: Add an exhibit listing subprocessors with region and data-access level; include mechanism for onshore-only routing and periodic attestations (quarterly).

I'll prepare a short redline to your PDF and propose the above language; will aim to send the redline within 3 business days. If Medicore requires DocuSign-ready language we can provide a negotiated addendum (Deal ID MED-2319).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

question: When a production model experiment shows a sustained increase in harmful output warnings for two evaluation windows, what automated actions should the platform take regarding traffic shifting and incident/oncall notifications?

gold_documents.text:
Acceptance matrix for Optimize quality shocks and auto-remediation

Purpose: Define a prescriptive acceptance matrix and automated remediation paths for Optimize so that model rollouts and runtime changes that impact quality are detected rapidly, attributed to cohorts, and either automatically mitigated or escalated with clear human-in-the-loop steps. Scope covers promptset stratification, metric composition, regression thresholds, A/B stopping rules, automated fallback behavior, alerting semantics, and required instrumentation. Out of scope: model training pipelines and offline benchmark generation (handled by Research).
AC1: Promptset stratification defined and published: at minimum the system must support labeling prompts into four cohorts (core, long-tail, adversarial, customer-specific) with a mapping file stored in Drive and a canonical JSON schema for ingestion into the Optimize eval runner.
AC2: Minimum sample sizes and MDEs: For each cohort define a default minimum sample and Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE). Defaults: core=2000 samples (MDE 0.5%), long-tail=5000 samples (MDE 1.0%), adversarial=1000 samples (MDE 1.5%), customer-specific=min(300 or 5% of traffic) (MDE 2%). These numbers must be codified in the rollout config UI and respected by the canary harness.
AC3: Composite quality score and decomposition: Implement a composite quality score (0-100) composed of: relevance (40%), correctness (30%), safety/adversarial flags (20%), latency penalty (10%). Each submetric must be reported separately and in cohort view in the Console dashboard and in the canary API response.
AC4: Regression triggers: A canary must be marked as failing if any of the following occur within the observation window: absolute composite score drop >= 1.5 points for core cohort; relative composite drop >= 3% for long-tail; safety flag rate increase >= 2x and absolute increase >= 0.3% for any cohort. Safety regressions have higher priority and bypass soft cooldown gates.
AC5: A/B stopping rules: Implement a sequential Bayesian stopping test with the following rule: stop when posterior probability that candidate is worse than baseline by at least the cohort MDE > 95% OR when posterior probability candidate is better by >=95%. The harness must support an optional frequentist alpha=0.01 override configured per rollout.
AC6: Multi-signal decision lattice: The system must evaluate at least three signals (composite score, safety flags, latency P95) and apply a weighted decision lattice to determine action (continue, hold, partial rollback, full rollback). Weights must be configurable per project and default to composite>safety>latency.
AC7: Auto-remediation flows: If a critical regression (safety or composite drop > threshold) is detected and sustained for two consecutive evaluation windows, the platform must: (a) automatically shift traffic back to the last-known-good model for up to 75% of traffic, (b) open an incident in the tracking system with a pre-filled template, and (c) notify on-call via PagerDuty and the Console alerting channel.
AC8: Safe partial fallback: For non-critical regressions the platform must support partial fallback routing patterns (e.g., 20%, 50%, 75%) with automated cooldown windows (default: 30m, 2h, 24h). Rollout must include a manual override to freeze traffic and require assignee approval to proceed.
AC9: Operational telemetry: Canary runs must emit per-cohort time-series for composite score, submetrics, sample count, variance, posterior probabilities, and action taken. All metric names and units must be documented in the PRD and wired into the Console dashboard and the alerting rules.
AC10: Auditability and forensics: Every automated decision (hold, fallback, rollback) must be recorded in an immutable audit log with keys: rollout_id, model_version, cohort, window_start, window_end, metrics_snapshot, decision_reason, and runbook_link. The audit log must be exportable as CSV/JSON.
AC11: Acceptance test harness: Deliver a small-scale integration harness (GitHub PR) that can simulate injected regressions (synthetic safety flags, relevance drops) per cohort and validate that the stopping rules and auto-remediation fire as expected. Provide test vectors and expected outputs.
AC12: Documentation & runbooks: Publish a Console-runbook template and a short PRD section for product customers describing how Optimize will behave under quality shocks, expected notifications, and recommended customer configuration defaults.
AC13: Backward compatibility: Existing Optimize rollouts without explicit cohort configs must default to a single 'core' cohort with legacy thresholds, and behavior should be equivalent to current baseline unless customer opts-in to new stratified checks.
AC14: Privacy & compliance check: Ensure that storing of customer-specific prompt examples for cohorting conforms to data retention and PII rules; add a flag in the rollout config for 'retain_examples' (default false).
2026-02-22 - Arielle Chen: Draft PRD posted to Confluence; requesting early engineering review on Bayesian stopping choice. Link above.
2026-02-25 - Daniel Ortega (ENG): Reviewed thresholds. Suggest reducing core MDE to 0.4% for high-traffic customers; proposed opt-in knob in rollout config. See inline comment in PRD.
2026-03-01 - Maya Singh (PM): Accepted opt-in knob approach. Added acceptance criterion for backward compatibility and default legacy behavior.
2026-03-04 - Priya Rao (DS): Recommends Bayesian sequential test with hierarchical priors across cohorts to improve power for long-tail; will provide a notebook by 2026-03-10.
2026-03-07 - Legal (L. Morales): Confirmed that customer-specific prompt retention must be opt-in and documented for contracts; suggested retention defaults to 30 days. Added security_review_required=false for now but flagged for SOC sync.
2026-03-10 - Engineering lead (H. Park): Spike complete. Prototype harness validates auto-fallback for injected safety regressions; opened GH PR #312. Need instrumentation schema before enabling Console wiring.
2026-03-12 - Arielle Chen: Updated PRD with ACs and sample sizes after DS feedback. Ready for design review to surface the config controls in Console.
